definition: The engineering discipline of designing deterministic control structures, safety guardrails, and validation cycles around non-deterministic LLM iterations.
details: Loop engineering addresses failure modes in multi-step agent executions (such as infinite execution cycles, task drift, and semantic divergence) by implementing strict termination guarantees, state schema validation, and memory pruners.

explainer.lead: The discipline of wrapping deterministic control, guardrails, and validation around non-deterministic LLM iterations. It matters because multi-step agent runs otherwise suffer infinite cycles and task drift.

tiers.eli5: It's like putting a referee and a shot clock around a improviser, so the freewheeling play still ends on time and stays on script.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers add strict termination guarantees, state schema validation, and memory pruners to agent loops; a pitfall is omitting a hard stop, letting agents loop indefinitely or drift from the task.
tiers.paperLevel: Addresses failure modes of multi-step agent execution — infinite execution cycles, task drift, semantic divergence — via termination guarantees, state schema validation, and memory pruning.

explainer.example: An agent rewriting a document is capped at a fixed number of iterations and must pass a schema check on its output state before the next loop begins.

citation.title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning in Language Models
